draft.title: Kublai Khan and the Yuan dynasty
card: Kublai Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan. He became the Great Khan of the Mongols in 1260.
Kublai set out to rule China. The Mongols had already taken the north, and in 1279 his forces defeated the Song dynasty in the south. For the first time, all of China was ruled by foreigners.
In 1271 Kublai named his rule the Yuan dynasty. He made his capital at Khanbaliq, now Beijing.
Kublai ruled as a Chinese-style emperor and used some Chinese methods of government. The Yuan dynasty lasted until 1368, when it was overthrown.
draft.remember: Kublai Khan, Genghis Khan's grandson, conquered China and founded the Yuan dynasty, which ruled until 1368.

a.q: Who was Kublai Khan, and what did he found?
opts: Genghis Khan's grandson, who founded the Yuan dynasty
Genghis Khan's son, who founded the Yuan dynasty
Genghis Khan's grandson, who founded the Song dynasty
A Song emperor, who founded the Yuan dynasty
a.why: Kublai was a grandson of Genghis Khan, and he founded the Yuan dynasty in China. The Song were the rulers he defeated, so they were not his dynasty.
a.clue: Think of the family link, and of who ruled China before him.

b.q: Why was Kublai Khan's rule over all of China unusual in Chinese history?
opts: Foreigners from outside China ruled the whole country
The Song dynasty ruled the whole country for the first time
The Yuan dynasty lasted for more than a thousand years
Kublai moved his capital out of China to the steppe
b.why: After defeating the Song in 1279, Kublai made the Mongols the first foreign rulers of all China. The Yuan lasted until 1368, so it was far shorter than a thousand years, and Kublai's capital was Khanbaliq, in China.
b.clue: Who were the Mongols, compared with the Song?

a.best: Genghis Khan's grandson, who founded the Yuan dynasty

b.best: Foreigners from outside China ruled the whole country
